capability.summary: Read-only audit of local and remote-tracking branches already merged into the repository's current HEAD
capability.description: Runs `git -C <repo> branch -a --merged`, strips Git's current-branch marker from each nonblank output line, and returns the resulting candidate list. Despite the cleaner name, it never deletes, prunes, fetches, or otherwise changes branches or remotes.
capability.problem_space: Read-only discovery of branch names Git reports as merged into current HEAD; not branch deletion, remote cleanup, stale-branch age analysis, merged-PR detection, or repository mutation.

constraint.io_signature: Input: repo_path CLI argument, with the script defaulting to `.` when omitted; output: JSON list and count of `git branch -a --merged` lines or a path/Git error.
accepted_inputs: an existing local Git repository directory path
no CLI argument when the current working directory should be inspected through the declared `.` default
constraint.output_shape: Success: {status: "success", tool: "git", repo: string, merged_branch_count: integer, merged_branches: string[]}; entries are stripped nonblank lines from `git branch -a --merged` and may include the current local branch, remote-tracking names, and symbolic remote HEAD text. Non-existing repo path: {status: "error", message: string} and exit 2. Nonzero Git result: {status: "error", tool: "git", message: string} and exit 1. Missing Git executable, 30-second timeout, or other subprocess exceptions are uncaught and may produce a traceback instead of JSON.
limitations: despite the cleaner name, this is audit-only and performs no branch deletion, remote deletion, fetch, prune, checkout, or other Git mutation
merged means reachable from the repository's current HEAD according to `git branch -a --merged`; no target base branch or revision can be selected
does not exclude the current branch, protected branches, default branches, remote HEAD symbolic entries, or branches by age, ownership, or worktree use
remote-tracking information may be stale because the wrapper does not fetch or prune; it uses a fixed 30-second timeout and does not catch timeout or executable-not-found exceptions

output_contract.description: JSON read-only audit containing the count and raw names of local and remote-tracking branches Git reports merged into current HEAD; nothing is deleted.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: list branches already merged into the current Git HEAD
inspect local and remote-tracking cleanup candidates without deleting them
negative_intents: delete, prune, or clean local or remote Git branches
fetch remotes or refresh remote-tracking branch state
find stale branches by age or branches merged into a caller-selected base
